title: Same name: a leaving official, then a contractor’s chief or owner months later

beats.text: July 2023. A Public Health manager leaves the City.
103 days later, the Board approves a City contract. Its notice carries the same name.
This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: Each approved contract has a notice naming the contractor’s chief executive and owners.

visual.label: Notice of contract approval
visual.sub: names the chief executive, officers, directors and owners

beats.text: The screen found 6 former employees with rare names.

visual.label: former employees with a rare name

beats.text: Their old departments have paid 5 of those contractors at least 43.3 million dollars.

visual.label: paid to those 5 contractors since the first notice, by the screen’s table

beats.text: The first lead. The manager’s leaving statement gives 6 July 2023 as the leaving date.

visual.text: Public Health Manager VII · leaving date 6 July 2023 · filed 30 June 2024

beats.text: The notice for a contract approved 17 October lists the same name as chief executive.

visual.kicker: Notice · signed 20 October 2023 · outpatient HIV health services
visual.text: Mission Neighborhood Health Center · chief executive: the same name

beats.text: Of Mission Neighborhood Health Center.
Public Health paid it 6,860,848 dollars in fiscal 2024 to 2026.

visual.label: paid by Public Health, fiscal 2024 to 2026

beats.text: The records do not show whether this is the same person or two people with the same name.

visual.line: the records do not show whether this is the same person or two people with the same name

beats.text: For one year, a former employee may not contact the old department to influence it.

visual.line: for one year, a former employee may not contact the old department to influence it

beats.text: Whether any took place, the records don’t show.

cards: Whether the manager had a hand in the center’s contracts

beats.text: The second lead. An attorney on the City Attorney’s labor team leaves in June 2023.

visual.toLab: agreement with a firm of that surname

beats.text: 188 days later, the office has an agreement with a law firm bearing the same surname.

visual.toLab: agreement with a firm of that surname

beats.text: Its notice, signed in September 2024, lists the same full name as shareholder.

visual.kicker: Notice · signed 25 September 2024 · labor and employment work
visual.text: A law firm bearing the same surname · shareholder: the same full name

beats.text: The City Attorney pays a vendor under that full name.

visual.label: City Attorney payments to a vendor under that full name

beats.text: 292,510 dollars, in fiscal 2024 to 2026.

visual.label: paid by the City Attorney, fiscal 2024 to 2026

beats.text: Three records, one name. Whether that is one person or two, they do not show.

visual.sub: one name: the same person, or two?

beats.text: If the firm is hers, she may be finishing old matters. That can be sensible.

visual.label: Finishing her old matters?
visual.sub: the agreement and its list of matters are not on disk

beats.text: The third lead. None of the 6 names is on the Ethics Commission’s waiver list.

visual.label: Post-employment waivers
visual.sub: none of the 6 names is on the list

beats.text: So none was granted. That does not show one was required.

visual.line: Its absence shows that none was granted. It does not show that one was required.

beats.text: No rule is shown to have been broken, and no wrongdoing.

beats.text: What would settle it? The law firm’s agreement, and any Ethics Commission advice letters.

cards.what: The City Attorney’s agreement with the law firm, and its list of matters
Any advice letters or waiver requests at the Ethics Commission

beats.text: Leading a clinic after Public Health is a common move. The question is whether anyone checked.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
